cards.explanation: The answer is Teach us to pray. One of His disciples says, "Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples." (Luke 11:1). He doesn't ask for a miracle or a fancy speech. He asks about prayer, and I love that he just said it out loud, friends.

The answer is John the Baptist. The disciple says, "…just as John taught his disciples." (Luke 11:1). He points to another teacher's students and asks for the same thing. I respect a man who asks for what he wants.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "When you pray, say: ‘Father, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come." (Luke 11:2). The kingdom is in the prayer, but the first thing they call God is Father. That's the first word, friends, and it's a close one.

The answer is each day. Jesus says, "Give us each day our daily bread." (Luke 11:3). It's one day's bread at a time, like a batch that never has to last till next Tuesday. Honestly, friends, that's my kind of schedule.

The answer is forgive. The prayer says, "…for we also forgive everyone who sins against us." (Luke 11:4). The people asking God for forgiveness also say they forgive others. Forgiving is lighter to carry than a grudge, and I can tell you that from experience, bakers.
The answer is Temptation. The prayer closes with, "And lead us not into temptation." (Luke 11:4). That's the last request Jesus gives them, friends. It's short, and it's the finish.

The answer is True. The man says, "…because a friend of mine has come to me on a journey, and I have nothing to set before him." (Luke 11:6). A friend showed up from a trip, and the man had nothing to put in front of him. I'd have hidden in the pantry, honestly, bakers.
The answer is Do not bother me. The friend inside answers, "Do not bother me." (Luke 11:7). It's not the warmest welcome at midnight, friends, but it is a very honest one.

The answer is False. The man inside says, "My door is already shut, and my children and I are in bed. I cannot get up to give you anything." (Luke 11:7). The door and the bed are his reasons, and he never says he's out of bread. It's worth noticing what the text leaves out, bakers.

The answer is The man's persistence. Jesus says that even though he will not get up "…because of his friendship, yet because of the man’s persistence, he will get up…" (Luke 11:8). The man keeps asking, and that's what moves him. I know a few snooze buttons that could learn from this, friends.
The answer is As much as he needs. Luke 11:8 says he "…will get up and give him as much as he needs." The man asked for three loaves, and the friend gives what he needs. Not a crumb short, bakers.

The answer is door. Jesus says, "knock, and the door will be opened to you." (Luke 11:9). It's the same word as the shut door in the midnight story, where the friend says, "My door is already shut…" (Luke 11:7). Ask, seek, knock. Easy to remember, friends.
The answer is Everyone who asks. Jesus says, "For everyone who asks receives…" (Luke 11:10). Everyone is a very big word, friends, and it's the one He chose. I like a promise with no fine print.

The answer is False. Jesus asks, "What father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead? Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?" (Luke 11:11-12). He asks these as questions, bakers, and He doesn't say fathers do it.

The answer is True. Jesus tells them, "…if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children…" (Luke 11:13). He says it plainly, and He doesn't dress it up. I'd have winced, friends, but it sets up the best part right after.

The answer is He gives even more. Jesus says, "…how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!" (Luke 11:13). The gift He names is the Holy Spirit. The words "…how much more…" are right there, friends.

The answer is The Holy Spirit. Jesus says, "…how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!" (Luke 11:13). That's the gift He names at the end, bakers. Ask, and the Father gives.
